newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on weak won, high rates.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on weak won, high rates.

text.p: Stocks closed down for the sixth consecutive trading day on Tuesday as the weakening won and the rising interest rates hampered sentiment, brokers said.

"Fundamentals continued to worsen. A technical rebound is likely on Wednesday after a week-long consolidation, but overall sentiment shows no signs of recovery," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
The composite index closed 6.00 points lower at 741.29.
The won briefly hit the record low of 901.00 in the foreign exchange market before the central bank's repeated dollar-selling interventions.
Yields on the three-year corporate bonds, South Korea's benchmark interest rates, rose to 12.32 percent from 12.25 percent on Monday.

Brokers said the finance ministry's plan of additional sales abroad of shares in unlistng high-ranking Seoul officials, and authorities said an investigation has been going on to verify Hwang's testimonies.
Oh arrived in Pyongyang on Friday by train for "permanent residence", according to Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency's (KCNA).
South Korea's state television broadcast North Korean TV footage showing Oh stepping out of a train at Pyongyang railway station.

In an arrival statement, he hailed North Korean leader Kim Jong-il as a hero and slammed the South Korean government for pursuing policies hampering the reunification of the Korean peninsula divided at the end of World War Two.
The two Koreas have been locked in Cold War confrontation since the 1950-53 Korean war.
Volume totalled 31.61 million shares, compared with 28.98 million on Monday. Losers outpaced gainers 527 to 277 with 97 stocks unchanged.
Trading of primary blue chips were dull with buying limited to theme-backed shares.
KEPCO, which rose on Monday on bargain hunting, fell 200 won to 25,900. Samsung Electronics slid 100 won to 71,000 and POSCO fell 1,000 to 60,000 won.
Shares of Il-Yang Pharm rose 1,900 won to its daily upper-limit of 26,500 on a news report that the company had developed a raw material for semiconductors.

Il-Yang said the material, which will be used in production of one gigabit and four gigabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, would be supplied to Samsung Electronics, the world's leading memory chip maker.

Brokers said low levels of customer deposits with securities houses, now estimated at 3.08 trillion won against a yearly high of 3.6 trillion in mid-June, and rising loans for margin trading, valued at 3.3 trillion, was also eroding sentiment.
